_schema: Gate 1 Tier A — national tests. Methodology §2.1. Tests A1, A2, A4 are binary gates; A3 is scored 0-1 (see §2.1 rationale).

tests.A1_monetary_sovereignty: Own currency; freely floating; not a global reserve currency; not in a currency union. BINARY.
tests.A2_solvency: General government net debt/GDP <= 60% AND interest/revenue <= 10%. BINARY.
tests.A3_gold_as_export: Gold's share of national goods exports. SCORED 0-1, not gated — failing means the state has no stake in defending you, not that it will expropriate.
tests.A4_requisition: No confiscation, compulsory delivery, administered monopsony or gold-export prohibition currently in operation; any dormant power requires a new public legislative or executive instrument before activation; and compulsory acquisition provides a published compensation mechanism or judicial review. Historical use and ease of activation are disclosed residual risks, not automatic failures. BINARY.

countries.name: Australia

A1.note: AUD freely floating, non-reserve, commodity-linked. A small open commodity currency devalues continuously without policy intervention, so the state has no mechanical need to repress gold — the FX does the adjustment.

A2.note: Net debt ~18.8% (2025) and expected to remain ~20% per the May 2026 budget. Gross ~51%. Commonwealth gross debt A$977.7bn at 17 Jul 2026. Excludes Future Fund and RBA assets, so the true net position is stronger still.

A3.note: Gold has OVERTAKEN COAL as Australia's second-largest export by value, behind iron ore only — approximately A$68bn this financial year. The strongest single data point supporting the index thesis, and absent from v1.0.

A4.note: Banking Act 1959 (Cth) Part IV remains in the current compilation but is inactive under s40(1). Activation requires a new public Proclamation under s40(2). If compulsory delivery is activated, s44 provides either payment at a Reserve Bank-published price or a court compensation action. Passes the revised safeguards test; ease of activation and administered-price risk remain disclosed residual risks.

countries.constitutional_note: s51(xxxi) requires acquisition of property on just terms, with live precedent protecting mining tenements — Newcrest Mining v Commonwealth (1997) 190 CLR 513, where sterilisation of tenements by Kakadu proclamations was held an acquisition requiring compensation. CAVEAT: s51(xxxi) binds the Commonwealth, not the States. Mining tenure is granted under the WA Mining Act 1978 and state parliaments are not subject to the guarantee. Parked as an accepted risk (§11.1); it carries most of the residual jurisdictional risk in a ~100% Australian portfolio.

countries.name: New Zealand

A2.note: Gross debt moderate, well inside the threshold.

A3.note: Gold immaterial to NZ goods exports; dairy dominates. Low score, not a gate failure.

countries.verdict: PASS (3 of 3 binary tests, low A3 score)
countries.note: No eligible listed vehicle. OceanaGold is the only material NZ gold producer and its NZ assets (Macraes, Waihi) are a minority against Haile (US, ~315 koz 2026) and Didipio (Philippines, 80%-owned). NZ remains in the eligible set should a pure-play emerge. Fast-track Approvals Act 2024 fully operational; amendments Dec 2025 and Mar 2026 expanded scope — policy direction has hardened pro-mining.

countries.name: Canada

A2.note: General government gross debt above 100% of GDP in 2026 (federal plus provincial), grouped by the IMF with Italy, France, Belgium, the UK and the US. Net is materially lower owing to public pension assets, but the general government gross position fails the threshold as specified.

A3.note: Gold a significant but not dominant export.

A4.note: Foreign Exchange Control Act 1939-1951 required residents to surrender foreign exchange and gold. That history remains disclosed but is no longer an automatic failure under the revised A4 test; current-law activation and compensation safeguards require review.

countries.verdict: FAIL on A2 as currently recorded; A4 review pending
countries.note: Consequence: Red Lake (Evolution) and Sugar Zone (Vault) are ineligible ounces. Agnico Eagle excluded at entity level.

countries.name: Finland

A1.note: Euro member. No monetary sovereignty, no independent devaluation channel, and no exit. In an EU-level debt event Finland receives whatever the ECB and Council decide — Cyprus 2013 and Greece 2015 are the proof of concept for capital controls imposed on a member state.

A2.note: General government gross debt approximately 80% of GDP and rising.

countries.note: v1.0 treated Finland as eligible. Moot in practice — Rupert Resources, the only Finland-exposed constituent, delisted 16 Jun 2026 into Agnico Eagle. Separately, the Mined Minerals Tax (Act 1361/2025, effective 1 Jan 2026) raised the ad valorem rate on metallic ores 4.2x from 0.6% to 2.5% — not a Tier A failure but a 4.2x repricing of the state's claim, and exactly the fiscal-variance behaviour Tier B B2 exists to capture.

countries.name: United States

A1.note: Global reserve currency issuer. Unique motive — managing devaluation while defending reserve status — and unique tools.

A2.note: Net debt ~100% of GDP rising to just under 120% by 2029. Gross 126% in 2026 rising to 142% by 2031 — the largest absolute deterioration among advanced economies. Primary deficits averaging 6.7% of GDP for 2027-2031, against the ~3.5% associated with debt stabilisation.

A3.note: US gold output ~155-170 t/yr is immaterial to exports and the sector is politically small. No constituency defends it.

A4.note: EO 6102 (Apr 1933), the Gold Reserve Act (Jan 1934), and WPB Order L-208 (Oct 1942) remain material historical warnings but are no longer automatic failures under the revised A4 test; current-law activation and compensation safeguards require review.

countries.verdict: FAIL on A1 and A2; A4 review pending
countries.thesis_note: The realistic mechanism is not nationalisation of producers — US mine output at ~$20bn/yr against a $37tn debt stock is fiscally irrelevant. The prize is the stock: 8,133 t in the Treasury's gold certificate account still carried at $42.22/oz. Revaluing that requires touching no mining company. The risk to producers is monopsony purchase at an administered price, plus capital and export controls. Consequence for the index: Pogo (Northern Star) is ineligible ounces, and every US-domiciled producer is out.
